title: Compounded price-shock hiring sprint probe — 12-month sensitivity grid
content:
Executive summary:

This sheet is a tactical working probe to model the combined impact of abrupt customer price compression and an operational hiring surge over the following 12 months. Purpose: give CFO / Head of Finance a quick decision surface for (a) how many hires to pause or accelerate under price downmoves, (b) short-term Opex cushion required for a 12–24 week hiring sprint, and (c) sensitivity of gross margin to price moves at route- and feature-level.

High-level framing and use cases:
- Short, sharp price compression event: -10% / -20% / -35% realized average selling price (ASP) over baseline for 3 consecutive quarters.
- Hiring sprint: commit to 40–120 net new IC hires across Eng / SRE / Platform over 3 months to support Dedicated and Private ramp.
- Goal: map price shock to required headcount tuning to keep net margin above target bands (gross margin target = 55% baseline).

Key assumptions (working):
- Baseline annualized ARR contribution from projects in scope: $58,000,000.
- Baseline unit economics: token-driven variable cost equals 18% of revenue; fixed opex (SG&A + infra reserved) allocated to these routes = $12.5M annual.
- Median fully-burdened cost per new hire (first 12 months including ramp, tools, infra): $170k. Hiring efficiency (ramp to full productivity) = 20 weeks.
- GPU and cloud delta for Dedicated/Private capacity = $3.2M incremental if we hit the high surge scenario.
- Pricing shock modeled as persistent ASP delta for 9 months then partial recovery to -5% by month 12 for base scenarios.

12-month month-by-month staffing and cost grid (simplified CSV lines):

Interpretation notes for the above grid:
- Headcount cost delta column uses cumulative hires * 170k but fronts cost into early months to reflect recruiting spend and signing bonuses. Values in k$ (thousands).
- GPU/cloud delta is an incremental operating bucket for Dedicated/Private expansion tied to surge capacity (burst GPU pools + on-prem setup costs).
- Revenue shock column shows ASP-reduced revenue where scenario is -10% realized on baseline months 02–06, -20% months 07–09, and recovery to -5% by month 12 in the base shock run.

Sensitivity slices (precomputed from the sheet):
- Case A (base surge, no price change): Cumulative 80 hires, incremental opex = $17.0M, revenue = $62.2M, gross margin = 52% (below 55% target).
- Case B (-10% ASP persist 9 months): revenue -$5.6M vs base; to restore margin to 55% we'd need to reduce hiring by ~22 hires (delay or convert to contractors) OR cut GPU/cloud delta by ~40%.
- Case C (-20% ASP persist 9 months): revenue -$11.9M vs base; required mitigation = pause hiring entirely and seek $6M non-core cost reductions (reno, travel, 3rd-party licensing) to keep runway intact for planned product investments.
- Case D (-35% ASP tail event): immediate emergency protocol: pause >60 hires, negotiate ARR-level price floors with top enterprise customers, deploy temporary discount surcharges on burst capacity.

Micro-route sensitivity (example routes):
- Hosted API (volume-heavy): high elasticity to ASP changes; losing 10% price here reduces contribution margin faster because variable token costs scale.
- Dedicated (commit-heavy): lower direct elasticity due to multi-month reserved contracts; downside is lagged (customers may churn at next renewal).
- Private (on-prem / regulated): lowest elasticity; price moves drive sales cycle longer but conversion/profit per deal stays high.

Decision levers and rapid experiments to reduce uncertainty:
1) Hiring phasing: move from 3-month burst to 3x 4-week micro-sprints; pause after each sprint and reassess realized ASP.
2) Offer temporary contractor-only pipeline for last-mile infra hires to reduce sunk fixed-cost while preserving throughput.
3) Price-fencing experiments: small pilots of price floors for enterprise customers and a short-term volume discount for self-serve tiers to protect conversion velocity.
4) GPU/capacity deferral playbook: triage non-customer-bound capacity and shift to spot or pre-emptible instances for 60% of surge pool.
5) Cost recovery triggers: tie hiring checkpoints to realized average ASP and net margin locked via monthly dashboard (if ASP < -12% vs baseline for 2 consecutive months, hiring paused).

Open questions / risks to validate quickly:
- How sticky is ASP compression? (get cohort-level churn & renewal windows from Sales)
- Can we convert planned Dedicated capacity into staged rollouts to avoid full GPU commitment?
- Hiring pipeline composition: what fraction are junior vs senior where ramp differs materially?

Next steps (action items):
- Finance: produce full P&L waterfall by route for the three shock cases above; add weekly dashboard wiring (owner: Sofia). Due: 2026-11-22.
- GTM / Sales: provide renewal cadence and top-20 renewal revenue exposure list (owner: Liam). Due: 2026-11-12.
- Eng / Infra: map surge GPU demand into concrete SKUs and deferred-cost options (owner: Meera). Due: 2026-11-18.

Appendix: quick math snippets used in the sheet:
- Required hires to offset revenue delta = ceil(revenue_delta / (ARPU uplift per hire)) — ARPU uplift per hire here estimated at $540k annual at full productivity (very coarse).
- Break-even headcount reduction for -10% ASP case = ~22 hires (approx) computed by taking lost gross contribution / fully-burdened hire run-rate.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a working spreadsheet export — assumptions are aggressive and front-loaded to stress-test product/ops coupling.
- Please comment inline on Confluence page (linked above) and flag any route-specific revenue mechanics we should fold into the model.

Document history and provenance:
- Created by: Michael Chen (Finance) — initial working probe based on Q3 throughput metrics and a recent Sales warning about price pressure in EU enterprise trials.
- Collab: Sofia A. (FP&A), Liam O. (Sales Ops), Meera S. (Infra planning).

End of sheet.
